question: Which of the following is the largest freshwater lake in India by surface area?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Wular Lake**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Wular Lake** is the largest freshwater lake in India, located in the state of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It has a surface area of approximately **200 square kilometers**, which can vary depending on the season and water inflow.
 
• The lake is fed by the **Jhelum River**, one of the major rivers in the region.
 
• Wular Lake plays a crucial role in maintaining the ecological balance by acting as a natural flood reservoir for the Jhelum River.
 
• The surrounding area of Wular Lake is rich in biodiversity, supporting a wide variety of flora and fauna, including migratory birds and aquatic species.
 
• It is also a significant source of livelihood for local communities, providing opportunities for fishing, agriculture, and tourism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dal Lake:**

 
 
• Dal Lake is located in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, and is often referred to as the "Jewel in the crown of Kashmir."
 
• It is famous for its houseboats, shikaras, and floating gardens.
 
• While it is a prominent tourist attraction, it is not the largest freshwater lake in India.
 
 
 
• **Loktak Lake:**
 
 
• Loktak Lake is situated in Manipur and is known for its **phumdis** (heterogeneous mass of vegetation and soil that floats on water).
 
• It is the largest freshwater lake in northeast India and home to Keibul Lamjao National Park, the only floating national park in the world.
 
• It plays a vital role in the economy and ecology of the region, but it is smaller in surface area compared to Wular Lake.
 
 
 
• **Nainital Lake:**
 
 
• Nainital Lake is located in the town of Nainital, Uttarakhand, and is surrounded by hills.
 
• It is a natural freshwater lake shaped like a kidney and is a popular tourist destination.
 
• Though picturesque and culturally significant, it is much smaller in comparison to Wular Lake.
 
 
 
• **Freshwater Lakes:**
 
 
• Freshwater lakes are bodies of water with a low concentration of dissolved salts, making them suitable for supporting various aquatic and terrestrial life forms.
 
• India hosts several notable freshwater lakes, including Wular Lake, Dal Lake, and Loktak Lake, each contributing to regional biodiversity and economy.
